name: Shaphat
overview: Shaphat is a male figure known primarily as the father of the prophet Elisha. The biblical record does not specify his tribal affiliation or any additional personal details beyond this familial connection. His mention is concise, highlighting his role in the lineage of a significant prophetic figure.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphat means 'he judges' in Hebrew. This proper name is noted without indication that it was given directly by God, simply identifying the individual who is referenced in 1 Kings 19:16.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shaphat as the father of Elisha, the prophet, as inferred from 1 Kings 19:16. Beyond this, there are no other family relationships documented for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphat's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily derived from his role as the father of Elisha, who is a prominent prophet in Israel's history. His mention in 1 Kings 19:16 places him within the prophetic lineage that God uses to guide His people. Although Shaphat himself is not the focus of direct divine activity, his connection to Elisha links him to the unfolding of God's redemptive plan through the prophets.
